doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Musicians in Teddy Powell's band and waltz sets in Boston
summary: Boots Mussulli, Pete Condoli and others in Powell's band; playing waltz sets in Boston.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Charlie had already left I think. But that band was great. We had a marvelous player. We had a guy named Boots Mussulli, and Boots was my roommate and he would say to me, he had to write an arrangement a week for the band, and he’d say “what do you want me to write?” He didn’t know what to— I’d say “why don’t you do ‘Perdido’?” “Good, I’ll put a solo in there for you.” I’d say of course. He was beautiful. We had Pete Condoli with the band, Milt Bernhardt, two brothers, the Brooks brothers, lead trumpet and lead trombone. They were fantastic. Larry Brooks and I forget the trumpet player’s name. These guys were great. And who else did we have? Charlie Ventura, we had some good guys — all I know is good men. And we used to go up to Boston a lot and play the Raymour Playmore Ballroom, and, who am I talking about? Teddy Powell’s band?

Oh Teddy Powell’s band. Forgive me, it’s my age. But we used to play the Raymour Playmore Ballroom in Boston. And in those days every band had to do a waltz set, play a waltz occasionally, and we would play the waltzes and Charlie Ventura would say “A flat,” and we’d play [scats]. We’d play “Mairzy Doats,” as a waltz, and it was great. It was great, Charlie was great. And the kids, they realized that Teddy Powell didn’t have any talent, and they used to come to us and say “you know this is one of the best bands © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
we’ve ever heard of in this ballroom. Can’t you get rid of that guy up front?” We said, “no, he’s the leader, he put us together.”
Well that wasn’t the only band that that was the case with, was it?
I always used to say if a guy doesn’t have talent he books them and he leads the band. Except for guys like Benny Goodman and Tommy Dorsey and people like that.
